title: shape-fingerprint flags ext.allowShock/allowMT (no adtype, no boolean pop key)

source.name: ortbtools Core pop-family shape-signal recognition contract (packages/core/non-iab-formats.js POP_SHAPE_FLAG_KEYS, mirrored in dialects/shape-fingerprint.js) — the product's own documented, in-repo mechanism for recognizing pop intent purely from vendor allow-flag presence, with no ext.adtype string and no boolean pop-named key at all
source.version: repo HEAD at session start, commit a61fc25
source.license: Internal product code (ortbtools); no third-party material copied. MIT for the original fixture values.
source.notes: Distinct mechanism from both the adtype-string-hint and the boolean-flag-hint siblings: POP_SHAPE_FLAG_KEYS is a P1 shape signal — presence of any of allowMT/allowLayer/allowShock/viewOnClick/directLink with a permissive value (bool/0/1/'0'/'1'/'true'/'false') is itself the pop tell, independent of the key's own name meaning 'pop'.

modifications: All IDs, domains, prices and timestamps independently authored.
device.ip uses TEST-NET 192.0.2.44; user.id is a clearly synthetic string.
offers.example.test / tracking.example.test / publisher.example.test are reserved .test hosts; no live host, tracker or subscriber identifier.
provenance.sanitized: No real visitor or subscriber data. IP 192.0.2.44 is TEST-NET-1; every identifier is a synthetic-fixture string; every URL uses a reserved .test hostname.

pairApplicability.note: A genuine oRTB auction pair: the response bid references the offered impression, ids match, and the shape-flag hint is a Core-recognized, non-vendor-attributed extension convention, not a proprietary wire wrapper.

device.ua: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

specNotes: packages/core/non-iab-formats.js POP_SHAPE_FLAG_KEYS treats presence of allowMT/allowShock with a permissive value as pop intent even though neither key name contains 'pop'; scanExtForFormatHints iterates the flag-key list in declared order (allowMT before allowShock), so with both present the resulting imp.non_standard_format finding lands at the first-matched key's path (imp[0].ext.allowMT), deduplicated by format name — only one INFO finding for the whole imp, not one per flag key.

This is exactly the P1 shape-signal path the file's own header describes: 'Lets pop RULES detect onclick/popunder traffic that carries only these markers (e.g. imp.ext.allowShock) and no canonical hint.'

The response bid re-declares only ext.allowShock=true (not allowMT) — packages/core/rules/pop-response/index.js's per-bid gate only needs ONE recognized hint on that specific bid's own ext to run admLooksLikePop against its adm.
window.open(...) is the second of the three accepted pop adm shapes documented in packages/core/rules/pop-response/index.js's header comment.

packages/core/crosscheck.js's pop-landing rule must match the window.open destination host against bid.adomain regardless of which pop-hint mechanism tagged the bid — a different landing domain (offers.example.test) than the sibling cases exercises this independently of any single hardcoded host.
Browser preview must not open a real popup or dispatch tracking.
notes: Plain `iab` dialect, deliberately not the `ext-rtb` vendor dialect used by the sibling EXADS/Kadam/PPCmate/Adon3 pop cases.

preview.limitation: pop script has no visual body
